title: Granada (Serenata)
description: The first piece in the Catalan composer Isaac Albéniz’s Suite española, a piano serenade meant to evoke Granada. It is now better known in its arrangement for guitar.

title: Recuerdos de la Alhambra
description: “Memories of the Alhambra,” written by the guitarist Francisco Tárrega after a visit to the palace. Its rapid repeated notes, called tremolo, are meant to sound like the water in the fountains.

title: Noches en los jardines de España: En el Generalife
description: The first movement of “Nights in the Gardens of Spain,” for piano and orchestra, set in the Generalife, the sultans’ summer palace. Falla moved to Granada in 1920 and lived in a small house below the Alhambra.

title: Granada
description: A song in praise of Granada by the Mexican songwriter Agustín Lara, who had never been there when he wrote it. Tenors from Mario Lanza to Plácido Domingo made it a standard.

title: Take This Waltz
description: Leonard Cohen’s English version of Lorca’s poem “Little Viennese Waltz.” Cohen said reading Lorca as a teenager made him a poet, and named his daughter Lorca.

title: Omega
place: Placeta de San Miguel Bajo, Albaicín
description: The title track of an album in which Enrique Morente, a flamenco singer from the Albaicín, and Lagartija Nick, a Granada rock band, set poems by Lorca and songs by Leonard Cohen. A statue of Morente stands in this square.
